facts.raw_span: A man in his 80s was brought to the emergency department after a cardiac arrest
the patient was last seen healthy by his family 4 hours earlier
then was found unresponsive and pulseless in the bathroom
He underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, receiving 4 doses of epinephrine intravenously and endotracheal tube intubation with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 10 minutes
Family later revealed he had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and had been complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation
A family member witnessed him struggling for air before losing consciousness
Initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity
Sinus rhythm at approximately 100 beats per minute
Right axis deviation
Prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1
No acute occlusions found
QT interval of 360 ms measurable in leads V4-V6
